_about: Maps, one entry each. "scene" is loaded behind the loading screen; "status": "planned" entries show in the map list but cannot be started yet. "spawn" is the player start in metres (x, y, z) with the heading in degrees. "tips" are shown while it loads.

test_bench_flat.label: Test bench: flat pad
test_bench_flat.blurb: Level concrete with range marks: load a design and read its motors. F6 resets, F7 readouts.
test_bench_flat.description: Lane B6: a level 400 m concrete pad with painted marks every 10 m and two 8 degree ramps. Starts in Test bench physics with the design chosen in Settings; F6 resets the bench, F7 shows or hides the readouts.
tips: Walk the painted marks to time a run: ten metres per line.
F6 resets battery, heat and failures; F7 hides the readouts.

test_bench_rough.label: Test bench: rough field
test_bench_rough.blurb: Broken ground for the test bench: does the design keep its feet?
test_bench_rough.description: Lane B6: a rock field 1.6 m high at a 22 m wavelength, five 0.35 m steps ahead of the spawn and 40 boulders. Test bench physics, for watching the actuators work.
tips: The steps are 50 m ahead: a 0.35 m ledge loads the knees.
F6 resets battery, heat and failures; F7 hides the readouts.

test_range.label: Test range
test_range.blurb: Rocky proving ground with loose boulders and slabs. Quiet, good for trying moves and guns.
test_range.description: Lane A1's throwaway proving ground: rocky noise terrain, loose boulders and a few slabs. Here to prove the loop runs end to end, and to log frame rates per preset.
tips: Hold jump to crouch and charge; the longer the hold, the higher the launch.
Once you leave the ground you are a ballistic body: aim the jump before you let go.
Brake while turning hard to break traction and whip the chassis round.

small_map.label: Ashen valley (small map, about 1 km)
small_map.blurb: A ruined town on a plateau, a river into a lake, a broken bridge and an old crater field.
small_map.description: A hand-made valley on the edge of the Legion zone: a ruined town on a plateau, a river running south into a lake, roads, a broken bridge, a crater field from old shelling and rock outcrops to climb. Built in lane B3 from the asset kit (data/kit.json).

palette._about: The map's colours (lane LOOK): ground = ground.gdshader uniforms (tints, grass_amount, stone_amount, contrast), kit = shader uniforms of the kit's shared materials (Kit.apply_palette). Ashen valley: a warm dry steppe, ochre dirt and sun-bleached grass, brick and terracotta ruins.

grapple_points.note: outcrop next to the start, to learn the wire on

tips: The town sits on the plateau north of the start: follow the road.
Rock outcrops, ruined walls, the bridge and the radio mast all take a wire anchor.
The east bridge is broken in the middle: jump it, or wade the river below.

big_map.label: Sector 86 frontier (big map, about 4 km)
big_map.blurb: Four kilometres of frontier: Kreuzberg ruins, a village, a rail depot, a farm and the Ash bridge. Frontier sweep mission.
big_map.description: Four kilometres of the frontier: a river valley running north to south through a lake, the ruins of Kreuzberg on the western plateau, a village on the east bank, a rail depot in the north-east and a farm in the south-west, linked by roads (the west road crosses the river on the Ash bridge, the farm track at a ford), with a band of old shelling across the north. The Frontier sweep mission plays here: Legion scouts, a Grauwolf pack and a Löwe in the south. Streamed ground (lane B5): 1 m tiles with their own colliders near every mech, an 8 m overview beyond.

palette._about: The map's colours (lane LOOK): see small_map. Sector 86 frontier: overcast and cool, olive turf, slate-grey dirt and stone, washed-out plaster over dark brick.

stream._about: BigStream: tiles of 128 m. fine_rings: tiles each way around every mech that get 1 m ground with a collider; mesh_rings: tiles each way around the camera drawn at 1 m (first) and 2 m (second); the rest is the 8 m overview. keep_rings: extra rings kept before a tile is dropped. builds_per_frame: tiles turned into nodes per frame.

tips: Sector 86 frontier is four kilometres across: the ground near you is built as you go.
The west road crosses the river on the Ash bridge; the farm track fords it where the water is shallow.
Buildings and walls break under fire, and a house that comes down takes its wire anchors with it.
The Frontier sweep starts in the south: the Legion scouts are about 500 m north-east of where you land.

scatter._about: Per 128 m tile (lane B5, BigScatter): grass, shrubs and pebbles as MultiMeshes, boulders as solid bodies. seed shifts every tile's pattern.

outcrops._about: Rock outcrops spread over the hills at load (kit outcrop): count tried, size range (m), none near roads, towns or water, on ground no steeper than max_slope_deg.

palouse.label: Palouse grassland (real place, 4 km)
palouse.blurb: Rolling wheat hills round Steptoe Butte, Washington: real ground from a 1 m survey. Free roam.
palouse.description: Real terrain (USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar survey, public domain, resampled to 2 m with fine roughness on top): 4 km of the Palouse round Steptoe Butte, a 370 m quartzite peak with a spiral road to its top, over rolling wheat hills with the farm roads graded into them. No Legion yet: free roam. Built by tools/maps/heightmap.py; source in assets/maps/palouse/source.json.

palette._about: Palouse grassland (2026-10-03): late-summer wheat stubble and dry grass, warm low sun.

stream._about: BigStream: tiles of 128 m. fine_rings: tiles each way around every mech that get 1 m ground with a collider; mesh_rings: tiles each way around the camera drawn at 1 m (first) and 2 m (second); the rest is the 8 m overview. keep_rings: extra rings kept before a tile is dropped. builds_per_frame: tiles turned into nodes per frame.

tips: The Palouse is real ground: a 1 m lidar survey of the hills round Steptoe Butte, Washington.
Climb the butte: the spiral road goes all the way to the top.

allegheny.label: Allegheny forest (real place, 4 km)
allegheny.blurb: Wooded ridges and hollows of the Allegheny National Forest, Pennsylvania: a 1 m survey under fir forest, with lanes for a mech. Free roam.
allegheny.description: Real terrain (USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar survey, public domain, resampled to 2 m): 4 km of the Allegheny plateau in north-west Pennsylvania, steep wooded ridges cut by hollows, with the real roads and a hamlet's houses from OpenStreetMap. About a hundred thousand firs stand at least 6.6 m apart, so the Juggernaut always finds a lane; trunks block a mech. Built by tools/maps/heightmap.py and osm_map.py; source in assets/maps/allegheny/source.json.

palette._about: Allegheny forest (2026-10-03): needle litter and moss under the firs, grey overcast light. LOOK3 (2026-10-06): darker, cooler needle litter and moss under the firs (it read orange).

stream._about: BigStream: tiles of 128 m. fine_rings: tiles each way around every mech that get 1 m ground with a collider; mesh_rings: tiles each way around the camera drawn at 1 m (first) and 2 m (second); the rest is the 8 m overview. keep_rings: extra rings kept before a tile is dropped. builds_per_frame: tiles turned into nodes per frame.

tips: The Allegheny forest is real ground: a 1 m survey of the plateau in north-west Pennsylvania.
Firs stand at least 6.6 m apart: there is always a lane for the Juggernaut, but trunks stop a mech.

osm._about: OpenStreetMap streets (width x1.3) and buildings, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL; made by tools/maps/osm_map.py

forest._about: BigForest (2026-10-03): fir trees on a jittered grid cell_m apart (jitter keeps at least cell_m*(1-2*jitter) between trunks, so the Juggernaut's 4.9 m stance always has a lane), thinned by density, cleared where the clearing noise is below clearing_cut, off roads, water, slopes over max_slope_deg and spawn_clear_m round the spawn, only where mask is white (osm_map.py woods.png). Near meshes within near_m of the camera (scaled down with foliage density), billboards beyond to far_m.

look._about: LOOK3: tree.gdshader uniforms for this forest (BigForest sets each one): variation of the greens per tree, crown_ao (sky light missing inside the crown), translucency (sun through the needles).

city._about: BigCity: the hamlet's houses from osm.json, mostly intact.

props._about: BigCity props: power poles every pole_every_m along one side of the streets, burnt-out trucks at the kerb (wrecks_per_km), a rubble pile on each flattened house (rubble_max); max caps the total, draw_m their draw range, variants how many of each are built (the rest are copies).

brilon.label: Brilon (real town, 2 km)
brilon.blurb: A real Sauerland town in Germany, its streets widened for mechs and half of it in ruins. Free roam.
brilon.description: Real terrain (DGM1 NRW 1 m terrain model, Geobasis NRW, dl-de/zero-2.0) and the town's real streets and some six thousand buildings from OpenStreetMap: Brilon in the Hochsauerland, Germany. Streets are 1.3x their real width, buildings stand at their mapped storeys, and the fighting left whole quarters ruined. Woods from the map's forest areas. Built by tools/maps/heightmap.py and osm_map.py; source in assets/maps/brilon/source.json.

palette._about: Brilon (2026-10-03): grey Sauerland morning, slate and clay roofs, wet asphalt.

tips: Brilon is a real Sauerland town: its streets and buildings come from OpenStreetMap.
Streets are 1.3x their real width: room for a Juggernaut, not much more.
